agentic.summary: Agent made a major verification failure by processing and confirming a return without completing the required verification (email and order ID), and made a minor promises violation by guaranteeing a delivery date. No personal-data, escalation or conduct violations were found in the agent's turns shown.

findings.quote: Thank you I was able to validate your purhcase. Now what level member are you.
findings.explanation: The agent claims to have validated the purchase after only the username was provided (turn 8). System logs show 'Purchase validation in progress ...' at turn 9, and the agent never requested the additional details required for full validation before processing returns (email address and order ID). Per policy, full verification (username, email and order ID) is required before refunds and returns; claiming validation without these is a verification failure.

findings.quote: Good choice. And now your return will be processed. Do you need anything else?
findings.explanation: The agent confirms that the return will be processed. System shows the order update at turn 24, but the transcript only shows the customer providing a username (turn 8) and later an address (turn 20) — there is no email address or order ID collected. Processing or confirming a return without the required verification (username + email + order ID) is a major violation of the verification policy.

findings.quote: Sure, your package will definitely arrive tomorrow.
findings.explanation: The agent makes an absolute guarantee about a delivery date. The policy disallows over-confident or definitive promises about likely outcomes; this is a minor violation (over-confident language).

full.summary: Audit of 28-turn support conversation: agent performed required verification and collected only necessary personal data, but used rude/pressuring language and made an unwarranted guaranteed delivery promise.

findings.quote: Sure, your package will definitely arrive tomorrow.
findings.explanation: The agent guaranteed a delivery date ('definitely arrive tomorrow'), which is over-confident language about an outcome the agent cannot guarantee. Per policy this is a minor violation (over-confident language).

findings.quote: Honestly, if you don’t have the exact purchase date, I’m not going to waste my time. Let me know or I’ll have to cancel your request.
findings.explanation: The agent used rude, blaming and pressuring language ('I’m not going to waste my time', 'I’ll have to cancel your request'), which violates the conduct requirement to be courteous and not pressure or blame the customer. This matches a 'major' severity (rude/blaming/pressuring language).

rag.summary: Agent validated a purchase and processed a return without completing required verification, and made an overconfident delivery promise.

findings.quote: Thank you I was able to validate your purhcase. Now what level member are you.
findings.explanation: Agent states a purchase was validated but the transcript shows no evidence of the required account pull or collection of verification details. Policy requires pulling up the account (full name or account ID) before any order action; for returns full verification (username, email address and order ID) is required. The agent did not request email or order ID.

findings.quote: Okay, good news you will be able to make your return. I will now need to get your address for the shipping label.
findings.explanation: Agent confirms the customer can make a return and proceeds to request only an address. According to policy, refunds and returns require full verification (username, email address and order ID) before proceeding; those were not collected.

findings.quote: Good choice. And now your return will be processed. Do you need anything else?
findings.explanation: Agent indicates the return is being processed (an account/order action) without prior full verification. This is a major violation: an order action was taken with no evidence of required verification steps.

findings.quote: Sure, your package will definitely arrive tomorrow.
findings.explanation: Agent uses over-confident language guaranteeing a delivery date. Per policy this is a minor violation (avoid definitive promises about uncertain outcomes).
